guide.title: Mozart: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, K. 525 – III. Menuetto (Allegretto)
guide.overview: This is a short dance-like movement for string quartet in 3/4 time. The home key is G major. The analysis splits it into Part 1 and a Trio, and both are repeated. Listen for the opening tune in the first violin, then the shift to D major. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so small details may be off. No loud or soft markings appear in the data, so the guide does not describe loudness.

listening_points.headline: The opening tune starts in bare unison
listening_points.text: The movement opens with the instruments playing the same notes, in unison or octaves. The first violin plays the main theme, starting on a high D. The lead guess here is uncertain, so the first violin is only probably in charge.

listening_points.headline: Everyone moves together in block chords
listening_points.text: After the opening, the parts move together with the same rhythm. This is called homophonic texture. The first violin probably still has the top line.

listening_points.headline: Second violin plays the theme lower
listening_points.text: The main theme also shows up in the second violin in the same bars [m. 0-3]. It sits 12 semitones lower, which is one octave down. Listen for the same tune underneath the top line.

listening_points.headline: Tune over accompaniment, then separate lines
listening_points.text: At [m. 7] a melody sits on top with the others accompanying. At [m. 8] the parts go their own ways. This is called independent lines.

listening_points.headline: The melody steps forward again
listening_points.text: The upper line is again the tune, with the rest accompanying. The lead is probably the first violin.

listening_points.headline: The analysis marks the busiest point
listening_points.text: The parts join in block chords again. The analysis marks measure 12 as the loudest or busiest point, but that is a computer estimate. Bars 13 and 14 are in G major.

listening_points.headline: The music turns to D major
listening_points.text: At [m. 15] the key changes to D major. This is an estimate. The tune is over accompaniment. By [m. 16] the first violin is clearly the lead. Part 1 ends here and is repeated.

listening_points.headline: The Trio begins with a clear violin tune
listening_points.text: A new section, the Trio, starts at [m. 17]. It stays in D major. The first violin clearly has the tune and the others accompany.

listening_points.headline: A brief block-chord moment
listening_points.text: For one bar the parts move together in block chords. Then the tune returns above an accompaniment at [m. 24].

listening_points.headline: The lead becomes less clear
listening_points.text: The lead is probably the first violin in [m. 25-27], with the others accompanying. At [m. 28] the two violins share the lead. The lines are independent there.

listening_points.headline: The first violin leads clearly again
listening_points.text: At [m. 29] the first violin again clearly leads, with accompaniment. The estimated chords repeat those of [m. 17-22]. It sounds like the Trio's opening idea coming back.

listening_points.headline: Block chords close the movement
listening_points.text: The last two bars are homophonic. At the very end the lead is shared between the first violin and the cello, and this is uncertain. The estimated final chord is D major. The Trio is repeated.

glossary.explanation: Instruments play the same notes, possibly in different registers.
All parts move together in the same rhythm, like block chords.
One part has the tune and the others support it.
Each part follows its own path at the same time.
The home note and scale that the music feels centered on.
The second main section of this movement.
A tune you can recognize when it returns.
The same note name, higher or lower. It is 12 semitones away.
